slides.title: Lights, Camera, Action…
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 5 English, Unit 9: Lights, Camera, Action… Unit 9 is about scripts: the writing that actors follow on a stage and in front of a camera. You will read “The Forest Guardians” first as a play script and then as a film script, comparing stage directions with camera directions such as pan, zoom and close-up. You will also study compound nouns like woodland, footpath and bamboo grove, and write and perform a short scene of your own. The unit story, “Nookwatch: The Forest Mission”, follows Amal and Sami as they help rescue an injured lemur at a woodland rescue centre. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Recognise the layout and features of a play script, including the cast list, character names, colons, dialogue and stage directions.
Explain the difference between a play script and a film script, using examples from both versions of “The Forest Guardians”.
Read stage directions accurately and locate upstage, downstage, centre stage and the entrances and exits they describe.
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to recognise the layout and features of a play script, including the cast list, character names, colons, dialogue and stage directions. You will also explain the difference between a play script and a film script, using examples from both versions of “The Forest Guardians”. You will also read stage directions accurately and locate upstage, downstage, centre stage and the entrances and exits they describe. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Language for precise thinking
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: nook, woodland, bamboo, groove, fertile, textbook. Listen to each pronunciation in the vocabulary lab, study its meaning in context, and use the word accurately in your own discussion and writing.

slides.title: Read critically
bullets: The Forest Guardians: a play script
The Forest Guardians: the same scene as a film script
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes The Forest Guardians: a play script and The Forest Guardians: the same scene as a film script. Read actively. Identify each text's central ideas, notice viewpoint and reliability, and support every inference with relevant evidence from the text.

slides.title: What a Compound Noun Is
bullets: A compound noun joins two or more words so that together they name one single thing. Knowing the parts lets you work out a new word without reaching for a...
slides.narration: The first language focus is What a Compound Noun Is. A compound noun joins two or more words so that together they name one single thing. Knowing the parts lets you work out a new word without reaching for a dictionary every time. Notice the structure in the model examples, then apply it deliberately in connected sentences and paragraphs.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Writing 1: Write Your Own Play Script Scene
Explain, support and improve your ideas
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1: Read the Script Aloud. Organise your ideas, use evidence and respond clearly to questions. In writing, you will plan, draft, check and revise. Use the success criteria before submitting your work.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the vocabulary lab, continue through reading and comprehension, apply the grammar focus, and complete the speaking and writing practices. Use AI English for hints and feedback any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
